title: Recover Binary Search Tree
signature: recoverTree(root: TreeNode) -> None  # fix in place
statement: Exactly two nodes of a BST had their values swapped by mistake. Recover the tree by swapping those two values back, without changing the structure. (The checker reads the tree after your function returns.)

hints.1_question: In a valid BST an in-order traversal is strictly increasing. What does the in-order sequence look like after two values are swapped?
hints.2_nudge: There will be one or two places where a value is larger than the next one. The first violation's larger value and the last violation's smaller value are the culprits.
hints.3_big_hint: Iterative in-order: when prev.val > cur.val: first = first or prev; second = cur. Finally swap first.val and second.val.

known_bugs.name: fixes only the first out-of-order pair
known_bugs.followup: If the two swapped values are far apart in the in-order order, how many violations are there, and does your code look at the second?

known_bugs.name: takes the wrong node for 'first'
known_bugs.followup: At a violation (prev > cur), which of the two nodes is out of place for the FIRST violation, and which for the LAST?

known_bugs.name: does nothing
known_bugs.followup: Does your function change the tree at all?

followups: Can you do it with O(1) space using Morris traversal?
Why can there be one or two violations?
